newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Voyager NZ launches cut rate fax service.
newsitem.headline: Voyager NZ launches cut rate fax service.

text.p: Internet provider Voyager New Zealand said on Friday it would launch a cut-rate fax service on December 15, which it said could reduce fax transmission costs by about half.
By making user of off-peak Internet times, which corresponds with prime business hours, Voyager said it would enable users to send faxes at off-peak charges.
The service uses "black boxes" Voyager has developed.
The box, called a global router, breaks the fax machine's connection to the Telecom line and determines whether the destination number would involve a national or international toll call.
For Voyager it creates a revenue stream from Internet circuits during business hours, the time when Internet activity is at its lowest, Voyager's managing director John O'Hara said.
Internet use rises dramatically after 5.30 p.m., peaking between 7 p.m. and 1 a.m., and an ordinary Internet session brings in around five to eight NZ cents a minute.
